subject: models with more than one type of likelihood AND an observation matrix

messages.author: 8dbb28b015bb7762
messages.subject: models with more than one type of likelihood AND an observation matrix
parts:
Hi all!

I'm trying to construct a pretty complicated model using both of this features.

I have two likelihoods in the 'observations space', so I arranged the observations in a two-column matrix with the alternating NAs and so on. (http://www.r-inla.org/models/tools#TOC-Models-with-more-than-one-type-of-l)

I should also stack my covariates in the same way, but the interesting part is that I need to use an Observation Matrix (http://www.r-inla.org/models/tools#TOC-Models-where-the-response-data-depe).
Actually, I use a different observation matrix for each of the submodels.

The way I thought it would work was to define an observation matrix like this:
A1 NA
NA A2
where A1 and A2 are the observation matrices corresponding to each of the submodels.

Hoping that if I define a covariate like idx=c(1:p, rep(NA, p)), when mapped to the obervations space it will be (A1%*%(1:p), NA, ..., NA). So I would get each covariate mapped to the right half of the dataset.

However, I get this error repeated several times:

file: smtp-taucs.c hgid: 4a2b4db6fa4a date: Wed Jan 04 17:53:31 2012 +0100 Function: GMRFLib_build_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 654, Thread: 0 Variable evaluates to NAN or INF. idx=(1414,1414). I will try to fix it...

and finally it aborts with:

taucs_malloc_stub fail to malloc 36514792 bytes
Aborted


Is this the right approach to using these two features at the same time?

Thanks!
        ƒacu.-

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: models with more than one type of likelihood AND an observation matrix
parts:
The r-inla program doesn't parse the A matrix and passes it to the C program "as is". So you need to use identity matrices (sparse matrices with ones on the diagonal) instead of NAs.  Otherwise, what you've done is correct - these two features work well together.  You can also use the inla.stack command, which should cover these cases.

Best wishes

Dan
